title: A single entomopathogenic nematode infection assay for Drosophila melanogaster larvae
author: Mallick, Kenney, et al.

steps.title: Prepare agarose plates
steps.instruction: Fill each well of three 96‑well plates with 100 µL of 1.25 % agarose gel, then allow the gel to cool for three hours.

steps.title: Add Drosophila larvae
steps.instruction: Place a single third‑instar D. melanogaster larva (w1118 strain) into each well of the cooled agarose plates.

steps.title: Apply infection treatments
steps.instruction: Treat the three plates as follows:

substeps.instruction: Control plate: add 10 µL sterile water to each well.
Single‑IJ plate: add 10 µL sterile water to each well, then place one infective juvenile (IJ) of either Steinernema carpocapsae or S. hermaphroditum into the water using a fine paintbrush.
Hundred‑IJ plate: pipette 10 µL sterile water containing 100 IJs of either S. carpocapsae or S. hermaphroditum into each well.

steps.title: Seal plates for incubation
steps.instruction: Cover each plate with Master clear real‑time PCR films (Eppendorf, Enfield, CT) and manually perforate the films to allow airflow.

steps.title: Incubate and monitor survival
steps.instruction: Place the sealed plates in an incubator set to 25 °C with a 12:12 h light/dark cycle; monitor larval survival every two hours for a total of 96 hours.

steps.title: Repeat experiments
steps.instruction: Perform the entire assay at least three independent times.

steps.title: Analyze survival data
steps.instruction: Record survival counts, generate Kaplan‑Meier survival curves in GraphPad Prism, and compare treatments using a log‑rank (Mantel–Cox) test.
